articles.title_original: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin
articles.title_zh: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin
facts_zh:
Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin
- Published
President Donald Trump has announced a deal to import Russian diesel into the US, as he faces mounting pressure to bring down fuel prices.
Trump said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately "to the American and global marketplace" followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.
The move on Friday sparked anger from Ukraine's President Volodymr Zelensky, who called it a gift to Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged".

articles.title_zh: US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
facts_zh:
US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
- Published
US immigration officials have defended officers who shot and wounded a man in his car in New York on Thursday while his five-year-old son was in the back seat.
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) chief Markwayne Mullin said officers opened fire while trying to arrest a man with a criminal history.
"We weren't aware the child was in the car," Mullin said, arguing that it was the man, Oscar Belgal, who had put his child in danger.

articles.title_zh: Thousands of security personnel deployed as Delhi braces for ‘cockroach’ protest
facts_zh:
Thousands of security personnel deployed as Delhi braces for ‘cockroach’ protest
- Published
Parts of the Indian capital, Delhi, have been turned into a fortress, with tens of thousands of security forces deployed, as the influential Gen Z-led "cockroach" movement has called for a major protest on Saturday.
The protesters are seeking electoral reforms and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters' lists.
The Election Commission has denied this and Kumar is yet to comment on the resignation demand.

Donald Trump has chosen conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary.

She previously had a brief stint as a spokeswoman at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Donald Trump's decision to import Russian fuel to the US represents a remarkable about-face from the president.
Just three weeks ago, Trump signed legislation to authorise fresh American sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas.
Now, Trump says, Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel to the US and world markets in the coming months.

articles.title_zh: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
facts_zh:
Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
- Published
Russian tech giant Yandex has said it was struggling to maintain services after two of its five data centres were struck by Ukrainian drones in the past two days.
Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the company runs the country's most popular search engine, as well as a food-ordering and taxi app used by tens of millions of people.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks were in response to weeks of Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centres.

articles.title_zh: US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condems as 'assault on rule of law'
facts_zh:
US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condems as 'assault on rule of law'
- Published
The Trump administration has unveiled sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it sees as a "rogue" institution.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans.
The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order.

A man named Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores has secured a narrow victory in Peru's local elections, exit polls show.
The candidate for the centre-left Ahora Nación party was elected mayor of Queropalca, a remote district in the Peruvian Andes.
Some 229 residents voted for the 45-year-old, putting him ahead of the second-place candidate from right-wing Renovación Popular Perú by just 25 votes.

facts_zh:
Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, wins Nobel Peace Prize
- Published
Former UN human rights chief and International Court of Justice judge Navi Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.
The South African judge was recognised "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", which paved the way for a "more comprehensive global legal order", the Nobel committee said.
Pillay, 85, has taken part in high-profile work considering allegations of human rights violations during a decades-long career, including in Rwanda, Myanmar and Gaza.

facts_zh:
Ethiopia warns Eritrea it will defend itself after troops cross border
- Published
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of an "all-out invasion" of its northern Tigray region and warned it will defend itself, days after residents told the BBC Eritrean troops had crossed into the country.
In a letter sent to the UN Security Council and seen by the BBC, Ethiopia's foreign minister called it a "blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia's inherent right to self-defence".
Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel responded by saying it was facing "an unprovoked war of aggression" from its neighbour.

Two Renoir paintings stolen from French museum are recovered

Two paintings by Auguste Renoir stolen a month ago from a museum in the south of France have been recovered, the local town hall has said.
The two works were seized on 8 September when thieves cut through a fence and smashed a window at the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, where the French impressionist had lived during his final years.
The local mayor praised authorities for recovering the paintings and said the news gave immense joy and profound relief.

Three Saudi Arabian nationals have been killed in two attacks on the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, the country's civil aviation authority has said, after Yemen's Houthis said they had targeted the facility.

Doctor accused of 1994 Rwanda genocide offences to face trial in UK
- Published
A doctor accused of a number of offences relating to the 1994 Rwanda genocide is set to face trial in autumn next year.
Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, is accused of "killing, directing or encouraging" the deaths of members of the Tutsi ethnic group in Rwanda.
He is the first person in the UK to have been charged over the genocide.

articles.title_zh: Crazy Rich Asians to return as TV show with original film's stars
facts_zh:
Crazy Rich Asians to return as TV show with original film's stars
- Published
Four of the stars of 2018's Crazy Rich Asians film are reprising their roles for a TV show of the same name.

The series will pick up events after the end of the hit film, with Constance Wu and Henry Golding playing their lead roles of Rachel and Nick, while Ronny Chieng is back as Eddie and Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh will have a recurring role as Nick's mother Eleanor.
"It's a 'Crazy Rich' family reunion!" said Adele Lim, who co-wrote the film, calling it the sequel we've been waiting for".

all_titles.en: Crazy Rich Asians to return as TV show with original film's stars

articles.title_original: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season
articles.title_zh: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season
facts_zh: Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb.
It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
As a result of the strong El Niño , it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season.

all_titles.en: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season

articles.title_original: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
articles.title_zh: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
facts_zh:
Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
- Published
Thieves have stolen 30,000 bottles of wine collectively worth about €5m (£4.2m) from a prestigious Italian winery, Italian media report.

Marchesi Antinori, one of Italy's biggest family-owned wineries, said the theft at its storage facility in Tuscany took place on Saturday as the company was preparing to ship a consignment to customers abroad.

At least seven masked men are believed to have deactivated the alarms, disabled the cameras and used company forklifts to load two large trucks of the company's prized Tignanello, Solaia and Guado al Tasso Tuscan reds.

all_titles.en: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
